items.title: Coroner walks out during Zara Qairina inquest after saying ‘Am I not fair enough?’ twice
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 26 — The Coroner’s Court hearing the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir saw a tense moment today when Coroner Judge Amir Shah Amir Hassan suddenly stood and left his bench after twice asking, “Am I not fair enough?” Datuk Rizwandean M. Borhan, representing Zara Qairina’s mother, then remarked that Ram’s questioning of Wong appeared harsh. Ram then said: “No, Sir.

items.title: Coordinated attacks: Thailand's southern insurgency flares
items.summary: A surge in attacks across Thailand's south has put a spotlight on the low-level insurgency by Muslim separatists that has killed thousands of people in the last two decades. Dozens of coordinated night-time attacks across the three southernmost provinces near Malaysia over the weekend injured three people and left government buildings and vehicles burned. These are the latest incidents of incendiary attacks in the long-running conflict in Thailand's far south.

items.title: Kuching airport repairs underway after storm damages ceiling
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 26 — Repair works have been carried out at Kuching International Airport (KIA) following damage to part of its external ceiling structure caused by severe weather on Tuesday. Malaysia Airports, in an update posted on its official Facebook page, said the affected area had been secured to allow the repair works to be carried out safely. “Repair works at KIA are underway on the section of the external ceiling structure affected by the severe weather earlier today (Tuesday),” it said.

items.title: Look beyond racial and political lines this Merdeka, urges Sultan of Selangor
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has urged Malaysians to use this year’s National Day celebrations to reinforce national unity by looking past racial, religious, and political divides. The Sultan had earlier consented to the Jalur Gemilang being hoisted at the Selangor State Flagpole throughout the commemorative period. “Although we differ in race, religion, language, political ideology and background, the Jalur Gemilang reminds us that we remain citizens of the same nation,” the Sultan said.

items.title: Chinese vacuum maker Dreame winds down carmaking project
items.summary: BEIJING: Chinese vacuum cleaner maker Dreame is winding down its electric-vehicle venture, which it launched with considerable fanfare in August 2025 with the stated goal of building "the world's fastest car", according to Chinese media reports. The reported wind-down represents a dramatic reversal for the venture, codenamed "Star Project", that Dreame had championed as a key expansion beyond home appliances, with plans to launch its first luxury EVs in 2027. Dreame added that it would concentrate on four core areas: smart homes, outdoor living, smart mobility and embodied AI, without specifically addressing reports that it was exiting vehicle development.

items.title: [UPDATED] RM15,000 bet behind Johor highway illegal race
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A RM15,000 bet was allegedly placed on the illegal motorcycle race that saw a group block part of the Second Link highway in Johor last Saturday. "Based on the suspects' statements, the illegal race involved a RM15,000 bet," he said when contacted today. Earlier today, a suspected illegal motorcycle racing "jockey" was among three men arrested after they allegedly tried to flee a police operation at a condominium in Sentul.

items.title: PetDagang's bumper commercial gains unlikely to recur in 2H26
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Dagangan Bhd's (PetDagang) commercial margins are expected to moderate in the second half of 2026 (2H FY26) as earlier price-lag gains reverse, with Brent crude prices rising towards US$90 per barrel. PetDagang posted earnings of RM387.2 million in Q2 FY26, bringing its 1H FY26 core net profit to RM677.6 million. HLIB maintained its "Buy" call on PetDagang with a target price of RM21.34.

items.title: 38 held over suspected migrant smuggling via Sungai Kelantan
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH: A Malaysian man suspected of being a migrant smuggler was arrested with 37 undocumented Myanmar nationals in Kampung Cina, Kota Bharu, yesterday. Kelantan Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Maritime Captain Kamal Mohamad said the arrests were made following intelligence on migrant smuggling activities through an illegal route along Sungai Kelantan. He said an MMEA patrol boat conducting an operation detected a speedboat moving suspiciously in the darkness near Kuala Besar around 5.20am.

items.title: WhatsApp ‘boss’ scam leaves Terengganu car dealership RM452,000 poorer
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 26 — A car dealership company suffered losses of RM452,000 after its clerk fell victim to a phone scam syndicate. Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 50-year-old finance clerk received a WhatsApp message last Monday from a suspect whom she believed to be the company owner. He said the suspect instructed the victim to provide the company’s account balance and make three separate transfers totalling RM452,000 to three different accounts on the same day.

items.title: China prepares for more heavy rain from back-to-back storms
items.summary: HONG KONG: China's coastal areas and southern regions are preparing for days of intense precipitation, with tens of thousands of people evacuated as Typhoon Narra tracks inland and another storm churns toward the country's eastern seaboard. Narra made landfall as a tropical storm on Tuesday evening in the southern island province of Hainan after lingering over the Beibu Gulf — also known as the Gulf of Tonkin — for several days, dumping heavy rain across Guangxi, Hainan and Guangdong. Narra and the accompanying Typhoon Saudel, alongside tropical cyclones Gaenari and Atsani, form a rare quartet of storms swirling simultaneously across the Northwest Pacific and South China Sea, according to China's Meteorological Administration.

items.title: Penang SPM candidate targeted in sexual cyberbullying gets Education Dept support, protection
items.summary: Its director Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad said appropriate steps had been taken to protect the identity of the 17-year-old student and ensure that the incident did not disrupt her preparations for the SPM examination. Mohamad Dziauddin said the school had also advised the student to seek guidance and counselling to help her manage her emotions and focus on her SPM preparations. He said JPNPP would continue to monitor the case and work with the school and parents to safeguard the student’s safety and wellbeing.

items.title: Elderly couple turn discarded bottles into National Month decor
items.summary: JERTIH: From piles of used plastic water bottles collected around an oil palm plantation, an elderly couple in Kampung Baru Tok Dor here have created colourful flower decorations for National Month celebrations. Their creativity has not only brightened the village but also showcased their patriotism while giving discarded materials a new lease of life. Halimah Said, 65, said she and her husband, Mat Ail Mamat, 78, began making the decorations on Aug 1 for a house decoration competition held in conjunction with National Month celebrations at village level.

items.title: Malaysian man, girlfriend nabbed in Medan over drug-laced vapes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian man and his Indonesian girlfriend were arrested in Medan, Indonesia, last week for trafficking vape products laced with drugs. The 22-year-old Malaysian and his 35-year-old partner were detained by police in a car at a parking lot in Deli Serdang, along with 29 vape pods containing liquid drugs. "Upon searching the vehicle, we found 24 vape pods containing drugs inside a backpack," he told a press conference.

items.title: Mamdani explains opposition to NYC event with leader of India's Hindu nationalist group
items.summary: WASHINGTON: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Tuesday he did not support an upcoming event in his city featuring the leader of the Hindu nationalist group that is the ideological parent of India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Mohan Bhagwat, chief of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), is scheduled to speak at a Manhattan event on Saturday, according to the event's website. The event's website casts the Aug 29 gathering as the "Universal Oneness Celebration" bringing together the Hindu American community.

items.title: One China policy: Understanding Malaysia’s position on Beijing and Taipei
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s remarks on Taiwan have brought renewed attention to Malaysia’s One China policy and its relations with Beijing and Taipei. Anwar later reiterated that Malaysia prefers a peaceful resolution and that its position under the One China policy remains unchanged since 1974. What is the ‘One China’ framework?

items.title: One dead, three injured after 4WD crashes into tree at Miri public park
items.summary: The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) said the 24-year-old man who died in the crash was trapped in the driver’s seat. The department said it received an emergency call at 3 am, prompting fire and rescue personnel from the Miri Fire and Rescue Station to be dispatched to the scene, about four kilometres from the station. The department said one passenger suffered serious injuries while two others sustained minor injuries in the incident, and all three received initial treatment from MOH personnel at the scene.

items.title: Three killed, three injured in Kunak crash
items.summary: District police chief Superintendent Rejali Ak Angong said the driver and two passengers were pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry medical personnel following the 6.03pm crash. He said the Perodua Viva was travelling from Kalabakan to Kampung Sungai Langgas with six people on board, including the driver, two adults and three children. Rejali said another passenger was seriously injured, while two others suffered minor injuries.

items.title: Three more nabbed over illegal race on Malaysia-Singapore Second Link
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Police have arrested three more men in Kuala Lumpur over a brazen illegal street race that brought traffic to a halt along the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link. Kulai police chief Tan Seng Lee said the latest arrests bring the total number of individuals detained in connection with the incident to 11, Kosmo reported. Police had earlier rounded up eight men on Sunday, including a motorsport influencer, obtaining a four-day remand order to facilitate investigations.

items.title: Malay unity should prioritise governance over electoral engineering
items.summary: LETTER: Musyawarah Nasional 2.0 demonstrated that Malay political cooperation has acquired a useful meeting place, but it did not establish a new political alignment. The Aug 25 forum in Kuala Lumpur was centred on Tabung Haji governance, not a negotiation among Malay parties. Its significance lies elsewhere: competing political figures could debate accountability without first agreeing on electoral partnership.

items.title: Inquest into Zara Qairina's death briefly halted after tense exchange
items.summary: Ram: "Don't use the word 'harsh' on me. Let's be fair. Ram: "You are fair, Tuan."

items.title: Three dead after Perodua Viva skids and crashes on Kunak-Semporna road
items.summary: KUNAK, Aug 26 — Three people were killed and three others injured after the car they were travelling in skidded and crashed at KM7 of Jalan Kunak-Semporna here yesterday. Kunak police chief Supt Rejali Ak Angong said in the 6.03 pm incident, the driver and two passengers were pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel from the Ministry of Health. Rejali said the accident also left one passenger seriously injured and two others with minor injuries.

items.title: Trump raises prospect of demolishing iconic Kennedy Centre
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration suggested Tuesday that the Kennedy Centre in Washington could be demolished if courts block his plans to overhaul the performing arts landmark. The extraordinary warning came in a Justice Department filing opposing efforts by Democrats to halt a two-year renovation and to prevent Trump's name being prominently added to the building. Trump's handpicked Kennedy Center board recently voted to place the words "Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump" beneath the institution's name and to rename its surrounding site the "President Donald J. Trump Plaza."

items.title: Selangor Sultan urges leaders not to exploit differences to divide Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has reminded leaders and politicians not to use political, racial or religious differences as an excuse to divide the people. The Sultan said while flying thousands of Jalur Gemilang during National Month was an easy task, the greater challenge was building a nation where every citizen felt respected, accepted and proud to be Malaysian. "Leaders and politicians should set an example by practising moderation, tolerance and compassion, and not use political, racial or religious differences as an excuse to divide the people," he said in a statement issued by Istana Alam Shah today.

items.title: ITMAX earnings seen setting new base as smart city rollout accelerates: HLIB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ITMAX System Bhd's quarterly earnings of around RM30 million could become the new base for the coming quarters, supported by its smart parking and CCTV businesses, according to Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB). Analyst Sam Jun Kit said the digital services infrastructure (DSI) segment also has room to grow in the second half of financial year 2026 (2H FY26), supported by the full contribution from MBJB smart parking, which started on May 1. On ITMAX's second-quarter earnings, Sam said the company's core profit after tax and minority interest (Patami) of RM30.5 million, up 16.7 per cent year-on-year, brought first-half core Patami to RM55 million, up 27.3 per cent year-on-year.

items.title: Missing Kafa teacher found safe in Kedah
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A Kafa teacher who was reported missing from Sungai Ara on Sunday was found safe in Pokok Sena, Kedah, early today. Mohamad Hijazi Zamri, 26, was reported missing on Aug 23 after leaving his home in Lilitan Sungai Ara at 8.40pm on a blue Yamaha LC135 motorcycle. Southwest district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said police traced him to a house in Kampung Bukit Payong, Mukim Gajah Mati, Pokok Sena.

items.title: Malaysia must move beyond reactive API readings to forecast haze, says air quality researcher
items.summary: KUALA NERUS, Aug 26 — Malaysia should develop an early haze warning system to protect public health following recurring episodes of air pollution or haze. Azman, who is also a researcher in air quality and environmental issues, said most of the data required to develop an early haze warning system was already available and could be integrated to enable haze risks to be detected earlier, thereby reducing respiratory-related illnesses. He added that a haze and health warning system could be developed by integrating hotspot data, satellite imagery, meteorological data, air trajectories, API readings, respiratory disease patterns and fine particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres in diameter (PM2.5).

items.title: Bersatu backs two Pahang reps' support for Wan Rosdy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu has taken note of two of its Pahang state assemblymen declaring support for Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail, party vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu said. Kuala Sentul assemblyman Datuk Jasri Jamaluddin and Lepar assemblyman Mohd Yazid Mohd Yunus pledged their support for Wan Rosdy through a memorandum of understanding signed by the menteri besar and both assemblymen. Jasri and Yazid pledged to support Wan Rosdy's administration until the 16th state election.

items.title: [UPDATED] Suspected 'jockey' among three nabbed after trying to flee police
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A suspected illegal motorcycle racing "jockey" was among three men arrested after they allegedly tried to flee a police operation at a condominium in Sentul. He said the arrests were made by the department's Intelligence and Operations Unit following investigations into a viral video showing an illegal motorcycle race on the Second Link highway in Johor. Hasbullah said the three were subsequently taken to the Kulai traffic police station in Johor to assist investigations.

items.title: Bersatu leadership approves two Pahang reps’ move to back Umno menteri besar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Two Bersatu assemblymen in Pahang have thrown their support behind Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail of Umno, with the party's top leadership signalling its backing for the move. Kuala Sentul assemblyman Datuk Jasri Jamaluddin and Lepar assemblyman Datuk Mohd Yazid Mohd Yunus — Bersatu's only two elected representatives in the 42-seat Pahang assembly — signed a memorandum of understanding with Wan Rosdy, pledging their backing for his administration until the next state election, expected by early 2028. Wan Rosdy has headed the Pahang state government since a hung assembly emerged from the November 2022 state election.

items.title: Penang Education Dept sets up haze ‘war room’, schools to switch to home learning once API hits 200
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — The Penang Education Department (JPNPP) will implement home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) in schools if the Air Pollutant Index (API) due to haze reaches 200. He said the department would assess API reading trends at four API monitoring stations in Penang, namely Minden, Balik Pulau, Seberang Jaya and Perai, at 6 pm or 8 pm the previous day to determine the necessary action for the following day. He said JPNPP had set up a ‘war room’ on Aug 13 to monitor the haze situation in the state from time to time, including developments in API readings, before informing the district education offices (PPD) to relay the information to schools in stages.

items.title: Trump orders US flags lowered for 'true loss' of Dolly Parton
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump on Wednesday ordered flags across the United States to be flown at half-mast for a week in honour of Dolly Parton, calling the country music legend's death a "true loss for millions of people". "Very sad to report that Dolly Parton, one of the greatest Country singers, and far beyond, EVER, has just passed away," Trump posted on his Truth Social network. Americans from all walks of life united in grief on Tuesday over the death of country music legend Dolly Parton, praising her music, philanthropy and film work.

items.title: Myanmar man charged with sexually assaulting 3-year-old Australian
items.summary: Aung Phyo Win, 30, claimed trial after the charge was read to him in Bahasa Melayu before Sessions Court Judge Juraidah Abbas. Deputy Public Prosecutor Anuarul Hakim Abdul Muen prosecuted, while lawyer K. Mahendran represented Aung Phyo. Earlier, Judge Juraidah asked Aung Phyo whether he could fully understand Bahasa Melayu.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM AUGUST 26, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened slightly higher today, tracking gains on Wall Street overnight as technology stocks recovered from a selloff ahead of Nvidia's results. Sentiment was also supported by lower oil prices and bond yields. The key index opened three points higher at 1,739.40 and is expected to hover between 1,730 and 1,740 today.

items.title: KLK gets mixed calls as analysts weigh earnings recovery against valuation
items.summary: The investment bank raised its target price to RM22.72 from RM21.97 after lifting its FY26 to FY28 core earnings forecasts by 1.8 per cent, 1.8 per cent and 4.7 per cent, respectively, mainly on higher crude palm oil (CPO) price assumptions. CIMB Securities analyst Ivy Ng Lee Fang raised KLK's target price to RM24.32 from RM23.70. She said KLK's third-quarter (Q3) core net profit fell 25 per cent year-on-year and 16 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM254 million, mainly due to higher associate losses.

items.title: NationGate hits one-year high as investors look past earnings slump
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Shares of NationGate Holdings Bhd jumped nearly 15 per cent to a one-year high in early trade, as optimism over its optical networking business outweighed weaker quarterly earnings. The electronics manufacturing services provider opened two per cent higher at RM1.52 from Monday's close of RM1.49 before climbing as much as 14.8 per cent to a morning high of RM1.71. Year to date, the stock has gained nearly 87 per cent.

items.title: Rantau Panjang ICQS sees fewer border movements amid Thai security concerns
items.summary: PASIR MAS: Movement through the Rantau Panjang Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex has dropped following bombings, shootings and arson attacks in three southern Thai provinces last Saturday. Rantau Panjang Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) commander Siti Khadijah Hamzah said 3,298 entries into Malaysia were recorded from Saturday to Monday, compared with 2,969 exits. She said incoming movements stood at 2,068 on Saturday before dropping to 1,230 over Sunday and Monday.

items.title: Firefighters contain half of 51.4ha Pengerang peat fire
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Firefighters have contained 25 hectares of a 51.4-hectare peat soil fire along Jalan Bypass Punggai-Sebana Cove here in Pengerang here, today. Johor Fire and Rescue Department operation commander Muhammad Tarmizi Md Jaafar said firefighting and firebreak operations were progressing smoothly, with teams maintaining 24-hour surveillance of the affected area. Drone units were also deployed to monitor the fire and track hotspots.

items.title: Indonesia's Destry Damayanti faces vetting for central bank's top job
items.summary: JAKARTA: Lawmakers in Indonesia will on Wednesday conduct a "fit and proper" hearing for Destry Damayanti, the sole candidate nominated for its central bank governor, who could become the first woman to take the top job. If given the green light, Destry, the current interim governor, would take charge at a tumultuous time in Indonesia, with concern lingering among businesses and investors about fiscal management, central bank autonomy, equity market transparency and the stewardship of the USUS$1.4 trillion G20 economy. Economists have said the Cornell-educated Destry, a senior Bank Indonesia deputy governor since 2019, would bring continuity to central bank policy and would prioritise stability while maintaining a good working relationship with the Prabowo administration.

items.title: BMW driver dies after crashing into parked cars in Bukit Mertajam, two others hurt
items.summary: Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis, in a statement today, said the department received a distress call about the crash at 2.31 am, before a team arrived at the scene nine minutes later. He said the crash involved a BMW, a Perodua Myvi and a Proton Persona. John said the injured BMW passenger and pedestrian were given initial treatment by the Health Ministry medical team before being taken to Seberang Jaya Hospital for further treatment.

items.title: Japan's corporate services inflation accelerates in July
items.summary: TOKYO: A key gauge of Japan's service-sector inflation rose 3.6 per cent in July from a year earlier, data showed on Wednesday, reinforcing the central bank's view that a tight labour market is pushing firms to pass rising costs on to consumers. The increase in the services producer price index, which tracks the prices companies charge each other for services, followed a revised 3.4 per cent gain in June, Bank of Japan data showed. Japan's core consumer inflation accelerated in July from a year earlier as firms passed on rising import costs from a weak yen and the US-Israeli war with Iran.

items.title: Japan to support alternative Mideast oil pipelines
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan plans to provide support for alternative pipelines in the Middle East as it seeks to improve energy security in the wake of the Iran war, local media reported Wednesday. Japan has already tapped its oil reserves to help cope with supply problems and increased crude imports from other countries including the United States. Other measures to be decided by a government meeting later Wednesday include an initiative for a special crude oil reserve to produce naphtha, broadcaster NHK reported.

items.title: Dollar moves in a narrow range ahead of inflation data, Jackson Hole
items.summary: SINGAPORE: The dollar was rangebound in early Asian trading on Wednesday as an uneasy calm hung over currency markets, with investors awaiting inflation reports from major economies including the US ahead of the Jackson Hole symposium this weekend. The Australian dollar was up 0.1 per cent at US$0.7172 after the release of data showing the trimmed mean CPI inflation measure rose at an annualised rate of 3.6 per cent. Its kiwi counterpart was down 0.2 per cent at US$0.5962 ahead of an interest rate decision from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand next Wednesday.

items.title: Dashcam footage surfaces of alleged fatal Shah Alam group fight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR : A dashcam recording believed to have captured part of a violent attack in Section 28, Shah Alam, which left one man dead and another seriously injured yesterday, has surfaced. Two men are then seen approaching the second victim. Shah Alam police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said police were alerted after a member of the public reported a fight involving a group of men.

items.title: Predawn blaze claims lives of father and nine-year-old son in Kuala Nerus
items.summary: Kuala Terengganu District Police Chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor, in a statement today, said police were alerted to a fire involving a semi-permanent two-storey house near Sekolah Kebangsaan Tok Jembal at about 4 am. He said the operation to extinguish the fire and rescue the 40-year-old man and his son was carried out by 16 personnel from the Kuala Nerus and Kuala Terengganu Fire and Rescue Stations. “A Fire and Rescue Tender (FRT) and a Compact Fire and Rescue Tender (CFRT) were also deployed for the operation,” he said.

items.title: Three die after Toyota Vios and Honda City collide on JB-Mersing road
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Aug 26 — Three people died after a two-vehicle crash at KM 80 of the Johor Bahru–Mersing Road on Monday evening, police said. Kota Tinggi OCPD Supt Yusof Othman said in a statement that police received a report of the accident at around 5:25pm. Police have appealed to members of the public with information on the crash to come forward to the Traffic Division at Kota Tinggi District Police Headquarters or any nearby police station.

items.title: Southern Thailand violence puts a damper on cross-border travel from Malaysia
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Aug 26 — Movement in and out of the Rantau Panjang Immigration, Customs, Quarantine, and Security (ICQS) Complex here has dropped following the bomb explosions, shootings, and building arson incidents in three southern Thai provinces last Saturday. Rantau Panjang Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) Commander Siti Khadijah Hamzah said that 3,298 movements entering Malaysia were recorded from Saturday to Monday, compared to 2,969 outgoing movements. “Outgoing movements, meanwhile, were recorded at 1,696 on Saturday and decreased to 1,273 on Sunday and Monday,” she told Bernama recently.

items.title: Sanusi to Ramkarpal: Come give Muslims a talk about not gambling
items.summary: Sanusi's remarks followed comments from Ramkarpal, who urged the state government to focus on educating Muslims against gambling rather than seeking ways to bypass a Federal Court ruling on commercial gaming licences. “We already have someone from DAP reminding us not to look for ways (to ban gambling in Kedah),” Sanusi said. Sanusi warned that approving licences for gaming outlets would spark widespread public backlash in Kedah.

items.title: Khairy seeks court order against MYNIC to uncover identity of ‘Corruption Watch’ author
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Former health minister Khairy Jamaluddin has launched legal action against national domain registry MYNIC Berhad in a bid to identify the owner of an online portal over an allegedly defamatory article. The disclosure application filed in court seeks the identity and corporate details of the registered owner behind the focusmalaysia.my domain name, following the publication of an article on March 10 titled “10 reasons Why KJ isn’t PM material, Malaysians must carefully examine his past track record”, NST reported. Through the pre-action discovery application, Khairy is requesting the registered owner’s identity card or company registration number, residential or business address, email, and contact number.

items.title: Penang police hunt missing Kafa teacher, 26, ahead of September wedding
items.summary: Southwest District Police Chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said that the police are also examining any information being circulated regarding the case. He added that members of the public with information regarding the whereabouts of Mohamad Hijazi Zamry, 26, are urged to channel it directly to the police at 04-8662222 or any nearby police station. Meanwhile, the victim’s father, Zamri Saidin, 53, said Muhammad Hijazi was reported missing after leaving to perform the Isyak prayers at a surau near his home.

items.title: Penang schools told to stay on alert as haze worsens
items.summary: JPNPP said it is monitoring haze developments and Air Pollutant Index (API) readings across the state, while schools have been told to monitor the readings continuously and remain alert to the latest warnings. “All outdoor activities must be stopped when the API reading exceeds 100, while schools must be closed immediately when the reading exceeds 200. JPNPP also instructed schools to ensure sufficient drinking water supplies, encourage students to drink enough water and reduce exposure to outdoor air.

items.title: Haze persists across Malaysia as 17 stations record unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Malaysia's air quality crisis showed no signs of abating this morning, with the Department of Environment's (DoE) MyEQMS portal recording 17 monitoring stations nationwide in the "Unhealthy" tier as at 8.45am today, as the prolonged haze episode stretched into another week. Sri Aman recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading nationwide at 167, followed closely by IPD Serian at 166 and Samarahan at 162, cementing Sarawak's status as the epicentre of the current haze crisis. Klang Valley smothered Six stations across Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya breached the unhealthy threshold as at 8.45am, reflecting the dense smog enveloping the greater Klang Valley conurbation.

items.title: Police nab one suspect after man dies in Shah Alam brawl
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — Police have arrested a man to assist in investigations into a fight involving several individuals in Taman Alam Megah here, believed to have occurred recently. Shah Alam District Police Chief ACP Sarudin Samah said the suspect was arrested following information received from the public regarding a fight involving a group of men in the area. “A review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed a group of men engaged in a fight, with several of them seen slashing one another.

items.title: Celebrity preacher, NGO secretary face charges over alleged RM12m misappropriation in Seremban court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will charge the chairman of a non-governmental organisation (NGO), who is also a celebrity preacher, at the Seremban Sessions Court today in connection with the alleged misappropriation of funds worth more than RM12 million. Following investigations, Negeri Sembilan MACC froze 15 accounts, comprising three personal accounts, three NGO accounts and nine company accounts, with a total value of about RM16.5 million. Also seized were three watches worth about RM5,000; three handbags (RM3,000); five bracelets (RM26,000); a ring (RM2,000); a necklace (RM7,000); and 51 one-gram gold pieces worth about RM31,000.

items.title: Buying strata? New housing policy proposes showing long-term maintenance costs upfront, tighter management rules
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Buying a strata property could eventually involve more than knowing the purchase price, monthly instalment and maintenance fee. With the recently launched National Housing Policy or Dasar Perumahan Negara (DRN) 2026-2035, the government proposes factoring longer-term maintenance and replacement costs into sale and purchase agreements for strata housing. It is among several measures in the DRN aimed at improving the long-term maintenance and management of housing, including better maintenance planning, professional building management and amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013 (Act 757).

items.title: MyKad printing services nationwide to face temporary disruption from tomorrow to Aug 31
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 25 — MyKad printing services nationwide are expected to experience temporary disruption starting tomorrow (Aug 26) until Aug 31 following the transition process to the new generation MyKad. The National Registration Department (JPN) said it was currently implementing the transition from the existing MyKad structure to the new generation identity card. “For first-time MyKad applications for 12-year-old children, parents or guardians are also encouraged to wait a while to enable their children to receive the new generation MyKad when production begins in the near future,” JPN said in a statement today.

items.title: Public toilets maintained, markets upgraded, drains improved: Housing Ministry says six initiatives surpass targets
items.summary: He said the public toilet maintenance initiative in PBT areas, which received an allocation of RM30 million, recorded the strongest performance at 734 per cent, with 367 projects successfully implemented compared with the original target of 50 projects. Nga said the construction of Madani stalls and upgrading of dilapidated public markets recorded an achievement rate of 170 per cent, with 102 projects implemented compared with the target of 60 projects, involving an allocation of RM60 million. Nga said the initiative to upgrade drainage and sewerage systems recorded an achievement rate of 102.67 per cent, with 154 projects implemented compared with the target of 150 projects, involving an allocation of RM55 million.

items.title: Sunway Lagoon says cooperating with authorities after roller coaster incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Sunway Theme Parks says that it is currently working closely and fully cooperating with all relevant authorities as they conduct a thorough investigation into the incident involving an attraction at Sunway Lagoon on Saturday, which affected 10 guests. Confirming the incident, the company also expressed deep regret, saying that their thoughts are with the guests and their families. “Sunway Theme Parks takes this matter extremely seriously.

items.title: Jeffrey Cheah says metal fatigue possible cause of Sunway Lagoon roller coaster incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 — Sunway Group founder Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah has reportedly confirmed a roller coaster accident that injured 10 people occurred at Sunway Lagoon on Saturday. The New Straits Times reported Cheah as saying authorities were investigating the incident, while he believed metal fatigue may have been a possible cause. Subang Jaya district police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat previously said 22 people, comprising Malaysians and foreign tourists aged between 11 and 44, were on the ride when the incident occurred at about 9pm on Saturday.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Weak 3.1-magnitude earthquake strikes off Batu Pahat
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 25 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.1 magnitude struck the waters off Batu Pahat, Johor, at 4.12pm today. In a statement, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the epicentre was located at coordinates 1.7 degrees north and 102.8 degrees east, about 18 kilometres (km) south-west of Batu Pahat. “There is no tsunami threat to Malaysia,” it said in the statement issued today by the National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre, MetMalaysia.
